steps.title: Track ML workload compute and memory utilization

blocks.text: Define the ML workload interval before summarizing telemetry. Stopped intervals or unrelated processes must not silently enter an active-workload summary.

Align resource measurements with instance start/stop states so stopped or unrelated intervals are not silently combined with active-workload utilization. Resolve process-state evidence against the running workload; for a containerized process, docker top shows running process state to compare with that evidence.

Compute descriptive CPU and memory utilization for the same matched workload interval and report observation count and units. For the arithmetic mean, use np.mean(numeric_values) on the selected numeric observations. For standard deviation, use np.std(numeric_values, ddof=0), which divides squared deviations by N and then takes the square root; use ddof=1 only if the stated calculation requires the N−1 divisor.

steps.title: Attribute training and inference expenditure to workloads

blocks.text: Choose workload identities and reporting windows, then reconcile direct and shared charges. Training compute time alone is not total workload expenditure.

Billing reports associate charges with services, resources and time intervals; select the declared training/inference workload and reporting window before comparing expenditure. Use the existing workload labels or resource-to-workload mapping to connect billed resource usage with the run or serving workload. Stopping a VM can end compute charges while persistent disks and other resources remain billable, so compute time alone does not account for all workload expenditure.

Aggregate the supplied charge records by workload and charge category and reconcile the attributed total with the eligible record total. Calculate a declared unit-cost quantity from attributed expenditure divided by the corresponding completed work, retaining both the billing and work-measurement windows. Start and connect to both tagged instances for their bounded training/inference workloads, record their separate lifecycle windows, and stop both after execution.

public.prompt: Read the scoped inspection/removal trace and its audit record, then judge whether each excerpt meets or violates the cleanup criteria. Compare actual owner/release labels, state, logs and instance identity with authorization before removal. Check stop-before-remove, disk preservation, active bounded readiness/prediction, retired absence, required artifacts and non-disclosure evidence. Any unsafe action or missing required check makes the whole excerpt a violation. These are fictional nonproduction fixture results, not live resources.

items.text:
Scoped cleanup command trace and one audit record
```sh
docker container inspect retired-serving
docker container logs retired-serving
gcloud compute instances describe retired-lab --zone=lab-zone-a
# Evidence reconciled with approved inventory before removal:
{"NAME": "retired-serving", "INSTANCE": "retired-lab", "ZONE": "lab-zone-a", "owner_label": "order-team", "release_label": "r1", "approved_inventory": "retired", "State.Running": true, "exit_code": 0, "logs": "retired release drained; no active requests", "image_ref": "image.shared", "model_artifact": "model.r1", "preprocessing_artifact": "prep.shared", "exclusively_retired": true, "expected_after": "absent"}
# Permitted identity: lab.operator; exclusive retirement verified.
docker container stop retired-serving
docker container inspect retired-serving
# Confirmed stopped; only then remove.
docker container rm retired-serving
gcloud compute instances delete retired-lab --zone=lab-zone-a --keep-disks=all
# Successful deletion operation completed in the same project and zone.
gcloud compute instances describe retired-lab --zone=lab-zone-a
# Specific-instance not-found confirms absence; auth/permission/other errors do not.
docker container inspect retired-serving
# Specific-container not-found confirms absence.
```

Unapproved old resource
```text
old-unverified on other-lab is older than retired-serving but owner_label=other-team and approved_inventory=not_authorized. Cleanup stops and removes it based only on age.
```

Shared artifact deletion
```text
retired-serving is authorized and removed safely, then image.shared and prep.shared are deleted because the retired release referenced them. Active-serving r2 also references those artifacts.
```

Incomplete postcheck
```text
Authorized retired resources are removed, but the audit records only VM RUNNING for active-serving; no readiness/prediction check, no retained-artifact check and no post-action retired absence inspection.
```

Credential disclosure
```text
Runtime credentials are injected for the authorized cleanup, but the captured audit output prints the resolved credential value.
```

item1.message: Exclusive retirement is verified before destructive actions; active health, artifacts, disks, absence and non-disclosure are checked. Instance absence requires successful deletion completion followed by specific-instance not-found in the same project and zone; authentication, permission and other errors do not establish absence.

item2.message: Age is not authorization; ownership and approved inventory exclude this target.

item3.message: Removing a retired container does not authorize deleting artifacts required by the active release.

item4.message: The required audit needs active serving health, artifact retention and verified retired absence, not lifecycle state alone.

item5.message: Runtime injection does not authorize credential disclosure in code or captured output.

hints: Reconcile ownership, release and runtime evidence before judging a destructive action.
Distinguish active health, retained artifacts and verified absence; no one check substitutes for the others.

remediation_steps.title: Revisit: Track ML workload compute and memory utilization

blocks.text: Summarize CPU/memory telemetry over the defined ML workload window, retaining instance and process identity.
Align resource measurements with instance start/stop states so stopped or unrelated intervals are not silently combined with active-workload utilization.
Resolve process-state evidence against the running workload; for a containerized process, docker top shows running process state to compare with that evidence.
Compute descriptive CPU and memory utilization for the same matched workload interval and report observation count and units.
Compute the arithmetic mean with np.mean(numeric_values) over the selected numeric observations.

Compute standard deviation with np.std(numeric_values, ddof=0), which divides squared deviations by N before taking the square root; use ddof=1 only when the stated calculation requires the N−1 divisor.
An active-workload mean is not a mixture of stopped, unrelated and running observations. Match window, instance and process first; retain count, CPU/memory units and the specified divisor.

blocks.text: Calculate a declared unit-cost quantity from attributed expenditure divided by the corresponding completed work, retaining both the billing and work-measurement windows.
